title: InlineUntypedPositions
description: Issue #139: a declared property and an array element typed from a keyword rather than from a "type" the sub-schema states, which is issue #137's narrowing in the two positions it left. `minimum` constrains numbers and is vacuous for every other JSON kind, so *float64 refused a string and an object in the decoder and []float64 measured a null's Go zero against the bound. The same follows from minLength (string), minItems (array) and required (object). Each keyword family appears in both positions, beside a sub-schema that does state its type -- which must keep narrowing -- and the $defs spelling, which has always had the wrapper.

num.$comment: The reported property. minimum says nothing about a string, an object or a null.

obj.$comment: An inferred object that is not a struct: `required` names no key of its own, so the property came out map[string]any and refused every scalar.

typedNum.$comment: The accept-control: the sub-schema states its type, so the narrowing is authorized and a string really is a rejection -- at decode, which counts.

viaRef.$comment: The same untyped sub-schema written as a $defs entry, which has always got the wrapper. The inline spelling must now agree with it.

numItems.$comment: The reported element position. ['abc'] died at decode and [null] was measured against the bound as the Go zero.

typedItems.$comment: The element accept-control, on the same terms as typedNum.

slot.$comment: The working sibling: a prefixItems slot has always been boxed, through the raw wrapper tupleItemDefFor names it with. It must not move.

nullableMap.$comment: A map value reached through the nullable arm rather than the plain one. #137 boxed the non-nullable spelling; this is its sibling, and it takes the same tail.
